import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Universal point sets

A universal point set of order $n$ is a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane on which every
$n$-vertex planar graph has a crossing-free straight-line drawing. The open problem asks whether
such sets can have subquadratic size.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Universal point set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_point_set)
-/

open Asymptotics Filter
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace UniversalPointSet

/-- A placement `p` of the vertices of `G` is a crossing-free straight-line drawing if it is
injective, no vertex lies in the interior of an edge, and the segments representing two distinct
edges intersect only at the image of a common endpoint. -/
def IsCrossingFreeStraightLineDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
    (∀ ⦃u v w : V⦄, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
    ∀ ⦃u v x y : V⦄, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y →
      ¬((u = x ∧ v = y) ∨ (u = y ∧ v = x)) →
      ∀ ⦃q : ℝ²⦄, q ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → q ∈ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) →
        ∃ z : V, (z = u ∨ z = v) ∧ (z = x ∨ z = y) ∧ q = p z

/-- A finite set `S` in the plane is universal for `n`-vertex planar graphs if every graph on
`Fin n` that has a crossing-free straight-line drawing has one whose vertex images lie in `S`. -/
def IsUniversalPointSet (n : ℕ) (S : Finset ℝ²) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
    (∃ p : Fin n → ℝ², IsCrossingFreeStraightLineDrawing G p) →
      ∃ p : Fin n → ℝ²,
        IsCrossingFreeStraightLineDrawing G p ∧ ∀ v, p v ∈ (S : Set ℝ²)

/--
**Universal point set problem.** Does there exist, for every $n$, an $n$-universal finite point
set in the Euclidean plane whose cardinality is $o(n^2)$? The point set may depend on $n$ and is
not required to lie on a grid.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem universal_point_set :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℝ²,
      (∀ n, IsUniversalPointSet n (S n)) ∧
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ ((S n).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n : ℕ ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2) := by
  sorry

end UniversalPointSet

Represented planar graphs as those admitting a crossing-free straight-line drawing. By Fáry's theorem this is extensionally the intended class of finite planar graphs, and neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib provides an abstract/topological planarity predicate.

Defined crossing-free drawings explicitly: vertex placement is injective, no non-endpoint vertex lies on an edge segment, and distinct edge segments may intersect only at the image of a shared endpoint. This also excludes edge overlaps and an edge passing through an isolated vertex.

Expressed the n-dependent point sets as a sequence `S : ℕ → Finset ℝ²` and subquadratic size as `(fun n ↦ ((S n).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ) ^ 2)`, giving little-o rather than only a quadratic bound.
Allowed arbitrary points of the Euclidean plane and imposed no grid or coordinate restrictions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Universal point set

A set $S$ of points in the Euclidean plane is *$n$-universal* if every planar graph on $n$
vertices has a plane straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at points of $S$.

Grids of size $O(n) \times O(n)$ are $n$-universal, and the smallest known $n$-universal point
sets have $n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$ points. The best known lower bounds are linear in $n$. It is an
open problem whether $n$-universal point sets of subquadratic size, i.e. of size $o(n^2)$, exist.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Universal point set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_point_set)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [CHK15] Cardinal, J., Hoffmann, M., Kusters, V., *On universal point sets for planar graphs*,
  J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 19 (2015), 529–547. [arXiv:1209.3594](https://arxiv.org/abs/1209.3594)
- [BCDE14] Bannister, M. J., Cheng, Z., Devanny, W. E., Eppstein, D., *Superpatterns and
  universal point sets*, J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 18 (2014), 177–209.
  [arXiv:1308.0403](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0403)
- [SSS20] Scheucher, M., Schrezenmaier, H., Steiner, R., *A note on universal point sets for
  planar graphs*, J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 24 (2020), 247–267.
  [arXiv:1811.06482](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06482)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

open Filter Asymptotics

namespace UniversalPointSet

/-- A *plane straight-line drawing* of a simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane is a map `p`
from the vertices of `G` to $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that
* distinct vertices are drawn as distinct points,
* no vertex lies on the closed segment drawn for an edge it is not incident to, and
* the closed segments drawn for two distinct edges meet only at (the images of) their common
  endpoints. -/
def IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
    (∀ a b v, G.Adj a b → v ≠ a → v ≠ b → p v ∉ segment ℝ (p a) (p b)) ∧
    ∀ a b c d, G.Adj a b → G.Adj c d → s(a, b) ≠ s(c, d) →
      segment ℝ (p a) (p b) ∩ segment ℝ (p c) (p d) ⊆ p '' ({a, b} ∩ {c, d})

/-- A simple graph is *planar* if it has a plane straight-line drawing in the Euclidean plane.
By Fáry's theorem this agrees with the usual (topological) notion of planarity for finite simple
graphs. -/
def IsPlanar {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : V → ℝ², IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing G p

/-- A finite set `S` of points in the Euclidean plane is *`n`-universal* if every planar graph on
`n` vertices has a plane straight-line drawing with all vertices placed at (distinct) points
of `S`. -/
def IsUniversal (S : Finset ℝ²) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsPlanar G →
    ∃ p : Fin n → ℝ², IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing G p ∧ ∀ v, p v ∈ S

/-- **Universal point sets of subquadratic size for planar graphs.**

Do there exist $n$-universal point sets of subquadratic size? That is, is there a sequence of
finite point sets $S_n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ such that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a
plane straight-line drawing with its vertices at points of $S_n$, and $|S_n| = o(n^2)$?

Equivalently, is the minimum size $f(n)$ of an $n$-universal point set $o(n^2)$? It is known that
$1.293 n - o(n) \le f(n) \le n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$ [SSS20, BCDE14]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem universal_point_set :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : ℕ → Finset ℝ², (∀ n, IsUniversal (S n) n) ∧
      (fun n => ((S n).card : ℝ)) =o[atTop] fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- The edgeless graph has a plane straight-line drawing precisely when the vertices are drawn as
distinct points. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem isPlaneStraightLineDrawing_bot {V : Type*} (p : V → ℝ²) :
    IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) p ↔ Function.Injective p := by
  simp [IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing]

/-- Every finite edgeless graph is planar. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem isPlanar_bot {V : Type*} [Finite V] : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  let f : V ↪ ℝ² :=
    (Finite.equivFin V).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.valEmbedding.trans (Infinite.natEmbedding ℝ²))
  exact ⟨f, (isPlaneStraightLineDrawing_bot f).2 f.injective⟩

/-- An `n`-universal point set has at least `n` points. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem IsUniversal.le_card {S : Finset ℝ²} {n : ℕ} (h : IsUniversal S n) : n ≤ S.card := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpS⟩ := h ⊥ isPlanar_bot
  have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (s := Finset.univ) p (fun v _ => hpS v) hp.1.injOn
  simpa using this

/-- Every point set is `0`-universal. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem isUniversal_zero (S : Finset ℝ²) : IsUniversal S 0 := by
  intro G _
  exact ⟨Fin.elim0, ⟨fun a => a.elim0, fun a => a.elim0, fun a => a.elim0⟩, fun v => v.elim0⟩

/-- Any two distinct points form a `2`-universal point set. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 52 68]
theorem isUniversal_pair {x y : ℝ²} (hxy : x ≠ y) : IsUniversal {x, y} 2 := by
  intro G _
  refine ⟨![x, y], ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro a b hab
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> simp_all [hxy.symm]
  · intro a b v hab hva hvb
    exfalso
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> fin_cases v <;> simp_all
  · intro a b c d hab hcd hne
    exfalso
    fin_cases a <;> fin_cases b <;> fin_cases c <;> fin_cases d <;> simp_all [Sym2.eq_swap]
  · intro v
    fin_cases v <;> simp

end UniversalPointSet

modeling_decisions: The terse list entry was read (per the decomposition notes and the Wikipedia article) as the yes/no question: do there exist, for every n, n-universal point sets S_n ⊆ ℝ² with |S_n| = o(n²)? This is equivalent to 'the minimum size f(n) of an n-universal set is o(n²)' (minimizers exist since universal sets exist, e.g. grids), but avoids `sInf` junk values; the docstring records the equivalence.
'Subquadratic' is formalized as `IsLittleO atTop` of n² over ℝ (little-o), not as 'below n²/4 − Θ(n)'.

Planarity is not in Mathlib. `IsPlanar G` is defined as the existence of a plane straight-line drawing in ℝ² (`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`, via the repo's scoped `ℝ²` notation). By Fáry's theorem this coincides with topological planarity for finite simple graphs, which is exactly the class the problem is about (graphs are `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`; every n-vertex planar graph is isomorphic to one of these and drawings transfer along isomorphisms).

`IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing G p` requires: p injective (distinct vertices at distinct points); no vertex lies on the closed segment of an edge it is not incident to; for two distinct edges (distinct as `Sym2` elements, so an edge is not compared with itself or its own reversal) the closed segments intersect only inside the image of their common endpoints. The 'vertex not on non-incident edge' condition is standard for plane drawings; it does not change the universality question (an isolated vertex on an edge can be handled by adding an edge, which preserves planarity), but it is included for a faithful notion of plane drawing.

Universal point sets are taken to be `Finset ℝ²` (finite), since the question is about their cardinality; `∀ v, p v ∈ S` places all vertices at points of S, and injectivity makes those points distinct.

  planar graphs*, J. Graph Algorithms Appl. 24 (2020), 247–267.
  [arXiv:1811.06482](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.06482)

A *universal point set of order $n$* is a set $S$ of points in the Euclidean plane such that every
$n$-vertex planar graph has a plane (crossing-free) straight-line drawing with all of its vertices
placed at points of $S$. Grids of $O(n) \times O(n)$ points are universal, so the minimum size
$f(n)$ of a universal point set of order $n$ satisfies $f(n) \le n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$ [BCDE14],
while the best known lower bound is $f(n) \ge 1.293n - o(n)$ [SSS20]. Whether there are universal
point sets of subquadratic size, i.e. whether $f(n) = o(n^2)$, is an open problem.

Mathlib has no notion of planarity, so this file defines planar graphs as those admitting a plane
straight-line drawing in $\mathbb{R}^2$; by Fáry's theorem this coincides with the topological
notion of planarity for finite graphs.
-/

namespace UniversalPointSet

open Asymptotics Filter
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {V : Type*}

/--
`f` is a *plane straight-line drawing* of the graph `G` in $\mathbb{R}^2$: the vertices are sent
to pairwise distinct points, each edge is represented by the closed segment between the images of
its endpoints, no vertex lies on the segment of an edge other than at its endpoints, and the
segments of two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
-/
def IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → f w ∈ segment ℝ (f u) (f v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  ∀ u v u' v', G.Adj u v → G.Adj u' v' → s(u, v) ≠ s(u', v') →
    segment ℝ (f u) (f v) ∩ segment ℝ (f u') (f v') ⊆ {f u, f v} ∩ {f u', f v'}

/--
A graph is *planar* if it has a plane straight-line drawing in $\mathbb{R}^2$. By Fáry's theorem,
for finite graphs this agrees with the usual topological definition of planarity.
-/
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℝ², IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing G f

/--
`S` is a *universal point set of order `n`*: every planar graph on `n` vertices has a plane
straight-line drawing with all of its vertices placed at (pairwise distinct) points of `S`.
-/
def IsUniversal (S : Set ℝ²) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), IsPlanar G →
    ∃ f : Fin n → ℝ², IsPlaneStraightLineDrawing G f ∧ ∀ v, f v ∈ S

/-- The edgeless graph on any countable vertex type is planar. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 52]
lemma isPlanar_bot [Countable V] : IsPlanar (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := Countable.exists_injective_nat V
  refine ⟨fun v => !₂[(g v : ℝ), 0], fun a b h => hg ?_, fun u v w h => h.elim,
    fun u v u' v' h => h.elim⟩
  have := congrArg (fun x : ℝ² => x 0) h
  simpa using this

/-- A universal point set of order `n` has at least `n` points. -/

lemma IsUniversal.le_card {S : Finset ℝ²} {n : ℕ} (hS : IsUniversal S n) : n ≤ S.card := by
  obtain ⟨f, ⟨hf, -⟩, hfS⟩ := hS ⊥ isPlanar_bot
  simpa using Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (s := Finset.univ) f (fun v _ => hfS v) hf.injOn

**Universal point sets of subquadratic size for planar graphs.**

$1.293n - o(n) \le f(n) \le n^2/4 - \Theta(n)$.
-/
